'''Katrin Leschke''' (born 1968){{r|born}} is a German mathematician specialising in [[differential geometry]] and known for her work on [[quaternionic analysis]] and [[Willmore surface]]s. She works in England as a reader in mathematics at the [[University of Leicester]],{{r|profile}} where she also heads the "Maths Meets Arts Tiger Team", an interdisciplinary group for the popularisation of mathematics,{{r|tiger}} and led the "m:iv" project of international collaboration on [[minimal surface]]s.{{r|miv}}

==Education and career==
Leschke did her undergraduate studies at [[Technische Universität Berlin]], and continued there for a PhD,{{r|profile}} which she completed in 1997. Her dissertation, ''Homogeneity and Canonical Connections of Isoparametric Manifolds'', was jointly supervised by Dirk Ferus and [[Ulrich Pinkall]].{{r|mg}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher at Technische Universität Berlin from 1997 to 2002, a visiting assistant professor at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]] from 2002 to 2005, and a researcher and temporary associate professor at the [[University of Augsburg]] from 2005 to 2007.{{r|lms}} At Augsburg, she completed her [[habilitation]],{{r|profile}} working in the group of [[Katrin Wendland]].{{r|wendland}} She joined the University of Leicester as New Blood Lecturer in 2007 and became reader there in 2016.{{r|lms}}

==Book==
Leschke is a coauthor of the book ''Conformal Geometry of Surfaces in <math>S^4</math> and Quaternions'' (Springer, 2002), developing the theory of [[quaternionic analysis]].{{r|cgs}}
